questions.stem: What did the boy from Central California do according to the report?
options: A) He set a record by swimming to and from an island.
B) He celebrated his ninth birthday on a small island.
C) He visited a prison located on a faraway island.
D) He swam around an island near San Francisco.

explain.定位:
A 9-year-old Central California boy braved strong currents and cold water to swim from San
Francisco to Alcatraz Island and back. A California television station in Fresno reported
Tuesday that James Savage set a record as the youngest swimmer to make the journey to the
former prison.
一名 9 岁的加州中部男孩顶着强劲水流和冰冷海水，从旧金山游到阿尔卡特拉斯岛再游回
来。弗雷斯诺的一家加州电视台周二报道，James Savage 创下了完成这一行程的最年轻游
泳者纪录。
explain.信号:
开头点题句即答案。新闻多在第一句就交代核心事件，swim from San Francisco to
Alcatraz Island and back 紧接着 set a record as the youngest swimmer，「往返游 +
创纪录」两点都落在开头，这正是新闻「首句点题」的信号，无需等到后面。
explain.替换:
swim from San Francisco to Alcatraz Island and back ↔ swimming to and from an island
往返游的同义改写
set a record ↔ set a record
破纪录原词对应
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音说他是 A 9-year-old（9 岁），B 把这个年龄数字偷换成 his ninth birthday（庆祝九
岁生日），原文只是交代年龄，根本没说过生日，是听到 ninth 就上钩的陷阱。
借用原文：A 9-year-old Central California boy
C) 原词陷阱
录音确实提到 the former prison（那座旧监狱，即目的地阿尔卡特拉斯岛），但男孩是
「游」到那里，不是 visited a prison（参观监狱）。C 借用了 prison 这个真词，却把动作
从「游泳」偷换成「参观」，答非所问。
借用原文：the former prison
D) 与原文相反
录音是 to Alcatraz Island and back（到岛上再返回），D 说成 swam around an island
（绕岛一圈游），方向被改了：往返 ≠ 环绕。San Francisco、island 这些原词都在，唯独
把关键的「往返」动作篡改了，与原文不符。
借用原文：to Alcatraz Island and back

questions.stem: What did the father do to encourage his son?
options: B) He set him an example.
C) He cheered him on all the way.
D) He had the event covered on TV.

explain.定位:
His father said he had offered his son $100 as a reward; to encourage his struggling son, he
doubled it to $200.
他父亲说，自己原本给儿子悬赏 100 美元；为了鼓励苦苦坚持的儿子，他把奖金翻倍到了
200 美元。
explain.信号:
encourage 后紧跟做法。题干的关键词 encourage 在录音里原样出现——to encourage
his struggling son, he doubled it to $200，「to encourage…」这个目的状语后面紧跟
的动作就是答案所在，听到 encourage 立刻锁定其后那句。
explain.替换:
he doubled it to $200 ↔ He doubled the reward.
doubled 指代同一动作
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
录音里父亲的做法是加钱（doubled it to $200），从没说他 set him an example（以身
作则做榜样）。这是原文根本没出现的内容，凭「父亲鼓励孩子常用树榜样」的常识硬套上
去就会中招。
C) 过度推断
cheered him on all the way（一路加油打气）听上去很像鼓励该有的样子，但录音里父亲
的具体动作是加倍奖金，并未说他全程喊加油，是把「鼓励」过度想象成喊口号的推断陷
阱。
D) 原词陷阱
录音确实出现 A California television station in Fresno reported（电视台作了报道），D
就借 TV 这个真词说父亲 had the event covered on TV（安排电视报道）。但电视报道是
媒体行为、与父亲鼓励儿子无关，更不是父亲安排的，是听到 TV 就选的典型原词陷阱。
借用原文：A California television station in Fresno reported Tuesday
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 On the 1st of January, new regulations will come into effect which eliminate an annual leave bonus
for people who put off marrying until the age of 23 for women, and 25 for men, the South China
Morning Post reports. The holiday bonus was designed to encourage young people to delay getting
married in line with China's one-child policy. But with that policy now being abolished, this holiday
incentive is no longer necessary, the government says. In Shanghai, a young couple at a marriage
registration office told the paper that they decided to register their marriage as soon as possible to take
advantage of the existing policy, because an extra holiday was a big deal for them. In Beijing, one
registration office had about 300 couples seeking to get married the day after the changes were
announced, rather than the usual number of between 70 and 80. But one lawyer tells the paper that the
changes still have to be adopted by local governments and these procedures take time. So people who
are rushing to register for marriage can relax.

questions.stem: What was the purpose of the annual leave bonus in China?
options: A) To end the one-child policy.
D) To give people more time to travel.

explain.定位:
The holiday bonus was designed to encourage young people to delay getting married in line
with China's one-child policy.
这项假期福利的设计初衷，是为了配合中国的独生子女政策，鼓励年轻人推迟结婚。
explain.信号:
目的信号 designed to。答案句靠目的信号词锁定：was designed to encourage young
people to delay getting married 里的 designed to 直接交代「设计它是为了……」，这
正是目的题要找的「用意句」。
explain.替换:
encourage young people to delay getting married ↔ encourage late marriage
「推迟结婚」概括为「晚婚」
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
A 项 To end the one-child policy. 把录音念到的原词 one-child policy 搬进选项制造「听
到就想选」。但录音说福利是「配合（in line with）」独生子女政策、不是「终结」它；真
正被废除的是政策本身另有交代，而非这项福利的目的。属原词陷阱。
借用原文：in line with China's one-child policy
C) 未提及
To increase working efficiency. 说的是「提高工作效率」，整段录音只谈结婚、政策与假
期，从头到尾没有一句涉及工作效率，属凭空捏造。
D) 过度推断
To give people more time to travel. 借录音里的 holiday（假期）顺势联想到「旅行」，
但录音说这是 annual leave bonus（年假福利）、其用意是鼓励晚婚，没有一处说给人时
间去旅行，属由原词过度推断。
借用原文：an annual leave bonus

questions.stem: What do we learn about the new regulations?
options: A) They will not be welcomed by young people.
B) They will help to popularize early marriage.
C) They will boost China's economic growth.
D) They will not come into immediate effect.

explain.定位:
But one lawyer tells the paper that the changes still have to be adopted by local governments
and these procedures take time. So people who are rushing to register for marriage can relax.
但一位律师告诉该报，这些变化还需经地方政府采纳，而这些程序需要时间。所以那些急着
去登记结婚的人可以放宽心了。
explain.信号:
转折 But 后才是真意。答案句靠转折信号锁定：前文一直在说新规将生效、人们抢着登记，
直到 But one lawyer tells the paper that the changes still have to be adopted by
local governments and these procedures take time 用 But 一转，才点出新规「还要走
地方程序、需要时间」这个真正落点。
explain.替换:
these procedures take time ↔ not come into immediate effect
「程序要时间」＝「不会立刻生效」
the changes still have to be adopted by local governments ↔ not come into immediate effect
「还需地方采纳」佐证未即时生效
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
They will not be welcomed by young people. 把录音念到的 young people 搬进选项。
但录音里年轻人是急着赶在新规前登记（about 300 couples seeking to get married），
并未表达「不欢迎新规」这种态度，选项凭原词反向编造，属原词陷阱兼与原文相反。
借用原文：300 couples seeking to get married
B) 与原文相反
They will help to popularize early marriage. 借了录音的 marriage 话题，却把方向反
了：录音原政策是鼓励 delay getting married（晚婚），新规取消该福利，更谈不上「推
广早婚」，选项与原文相反。
借用原文：encourage young people to delay getting married
C) 未提及
They will boost China's economic growth. 把话题硬拔高到「促进经济增长」，整段录音
只谈婚姻登记、假期福利与生效程序，没有一句涉及经济，属凭空添加。

questions.stem: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A) Cleaning service in great demand all over the world.
B) Two ladies giving up well-paid jobs to do cleaning.
C) A new company to clean up the mess after parties.
D) Cleaners gainfully employed at nights and weekends.

explain.定位:
Now, however, a New Zealand-based start-up company aims to bring messy homes—and
even splitting headaches—back to normal. The properly-named start-up Morning-After
Maids was launched about a month ago in Auckland by roommates Rebecca Foley and
Catherine Ashurst.
然而如今，一家位于新西兰的初创公司力图把一团乱的家——甚至连宿醉头痛——都恢复如
常。这家名字起得很贴切的初创公司"晨后女佣"（Morning-After Maids）大约一个月前在
奥克兰由室友丽贝卡·弗利和凯瑟琳·阿什赫斯特创办。
explain.信号:
转折 however 后引出全篇主角。新闻开头先说人人爱派对、但打扫不好玩，紧接 Now,
however, a New Zealand-based start-up company aims to bring messy homes...back
to normal 一个 however 转折，转折后冒出的"一家初创公司"就是全篇要讲的正题——主
旨题的落点常在开头转折之后。
explain.替换:
a New Zealand-based start-up company ↔ A new company
start-up = new company 同义概括
bring messy homes...back to normal ↔ clean up the mess after parties
把乱家恢复正常＝派对后打扫
explain.排除:
A) 过度推断
录音只说服务在本国 flooded with requests from across the country 并收到 from the
U.S. and Canada 的请求，A 却拔高成 all over the world（全世界都极度需求），范围被
无中生有地放大。
借用原文：Besides being flooded with requests from across the country, Foley and Ashurst have
also received requests from the U.S. and Canada
B) 与原文相反
B 说两人"放弃高薪工作"giving up well-paid jobs，但录音明说她们 they are both
gainfully employed（两人都有正经工作在身），只是把清洁活塞进晚上和周末，根本没辞
职。它借"工作"这个话题制造"听着像"，却与原文相反。
借用原文：Although they are both gainfully employed, they fit cleaning jobs into their nights
and weekends
D) 原词陷阱
D 的 at nights and weekends 和 gainfully employed 都是录音里 they fit cleaning jobs
into their nights and weekends 的原词，听到当然耳熟；可这只是"她们什么时候干活"的
一个细节，撑不起"整段主要讲什么"，对主旨题而言以偏概全。
借用原文：they fit cleaning jobs into their nights and weekends, which is when their service is in
most demand anyway

questions.stem: What is a common problem with a house party?
options: A) It takes a lot of time to prepare.
B) It leaves the house in a mess.
C) It makes party goers exhausted.
D) It creates noise and misconduct.

explain.定位:
Everyone loves a good house party, but the cleaning-up the next morning isn't as enjoyable.
人人都爱一场尽兴的家庭派对，但第二天早上的打扫就不那么让人开心了。
explain.信号:
转折 but 之后才是真问题。首句 Everyone loves a good house party, but the cleaning-
up the next morning isn't as enjoyable，but 之前是"人人爱派对"的铺垫，but 之后"第
二天得打扫"才是录音点出的派对麻烦——转折后才是答案所在。
explain.替换:
the cleaning-up the next morning ↔ leaves the house in a mess
需要打扫＝屋子被弄乱了
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
A 说派对 takes a lot of time to prepare（准备很费时），但录音通篇讲的是"事后打扫"，
对"事前准备"一字未提，属于无中生有。
C) 未提及
C 说派对 makes party goers exhausted（让参加者筋疲力尽），录音只提到为"恢复中的
寻欢者"recovering merrymakers 送咖啡和止痛药，并没说派对本身使人累垮，是借"派对
后状态"想象出来的，原文未提。
D) 未提及
D 说派对 creates noise and misconduct（造成噪音和失态行为），这是生活常识里派对
的坏处，听着很对，但录音从头到尾只谈"打扫"和"宿醉头痛"，没说噪音或失态，是拿常识
替代原文。

questions.stem: What are Rebecca Foley and Catherine Ashurst planning to do?
options: B) Visit the U.S. and Canada.

explain.定位:
They are reportedly meeting with lawyers to see how best to take the business forward.
据报道，她们正在与律师会面，商讨如何把这项业务最好地向前推进。
explain.信号:
结尾未来动作 take...forward 是落点。录音末句 They are reportedly meeting with
lawyers to see how best to take the business forward，take the business forward
（把业务向前推进）是指向未来的计划，正好回答"打算做什么"——新闻里"下一步"信息常
压在结尾。
explain.替换:
take the business forward ↔ Expand their business
把业务向前推进＝扩展业务
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
A 说"雇一名澳大利亚律师"Hire an Australian lawyer，录音确实念到 meeting with
lawyers（与律师会面），lawyer 一词耳熟；但录音只说"见律师"不是"雇律师"，更没说
是"澳大利亚的"——录音涉及的是美国、加拿大，澳大利亚是凭空加的。
借用原文：They are reportedly meeting with lawyers to see how best to take the business forward
B) 原词陷阱
B 说"去美国和加拿大"Visit the U.S. and Canada，录音确实有 received requests from
the U.S. and Canada（收到来自美加的请求），但那是"美加有人来请她们服务"，不是"她
们要去美加"，方向被偷换了。
借用原文：Foley and Ashurst have also received requests from the U.S. and Canada to provide
services there
C) 原词陷阱
C 说"了结一桩法律纠纷"Settle a legal dispute，它借录音 meeting with lawyers 里的"律
师"勾人；可她们见律师是为了"把业务推进"，录音根本没提任何法律纠纷，是听到"律师"就
脑补出"打官司"。
借用原文：They are reportedly meeting with lawyers to see how best to take the business forward

questions.stem: What did the man do yesterday?
options: A) He had a driving lesson.
B) He got his driver's license.
C) He took the driver's theory exam.
D) He passed the driver's road test.

explain.定位:
W: Kyle, how did your driver's theory exam go? It was yesterday, right?
女：凯尔，你的驾驶理论考试考得怎么样？是昨天考的，对吧？
explain.信号:
被问者话题由女方一句点破。答案不在男方的回答里、而在女方开场这句确认里——how
did your driver's theory exam go? It was yesterday, right? 直接点明"昨天"对应的事就
是 theory exam（理论考），男方随后用 Yes. 确认。开头的话题确认句是这种对话的定位
信号。
explain.替换:
your driver's theory exam ↔ the driver's theory exam
近乎原词对应
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
He had a driving lesson. 借用了对话后段反复出现的 lesson（驾驶课），但那是男方通过
理论考之后才开始的下一步，并非"昨天"做的事，时间对不上。
借用原文：I've only had two driving lessons so far
B) 过度推断
He got his driver's license. 是学车终点，但他刚过理论考、连路考都还没开始（后文还在
谈第一次路考的打算），远未拿到驾照，与"昨天"无关。
D) 原词陷阱
He passed the driver's road test. 盗用了对话里出现的 road test，但女方明说"下一步才
是路考"（all you have to do next is your road test），昨天考的是 theory exam 不是
road test，且"过了"更无从谈起。
借用原文：all you have to do next is your road test

questions.stem: Why did he fail the exam the first time?
options: A) He was not well prepared.
B) He did not get to the exam in time.
C) He was not used to the test format.
D) He did not follow the test procedure.

explain.定位:
W: ... I guess you underestimated how difficult it would be the first time, didn't you? I hear
a lot of people make that mistake and go in underprepared, but good job in passing the
second time.
女：……我猜你第一次是低估了它的难度，对吧？我听说很多人都犯这个错，去考的时候准
备不足，不过你第二次过了，干得好。
explain.信号:
女方点破"低估难度、准备不足"。原因不在男方自述里，而在女方一句推测点破：you
underestimated how difficult it would be the first time 与 go in underprepared 直接
把第一次失败归到"低估难度、准备不充分"。这种"我猜你是……对吧？"的推测应答句，正
是原因信号。
explain.替换:
go in underprepared ↔ not well prepared
underprepared=not well prepared
underestimated how difficult it would be ↔ not well prepared
低估难度→没准备够
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
He did not get to the exam in time. 说"没及时赶到考试"，原文通篇没提迟到或时间没赶
上，是凭空捏造的理由。
C) 未提及
He was not used to the test format. 说"不适应考试形式"，原文只说低估难度、准备不
足，从未提到"题型/形式不熟"，属另造原因。
D) 未提及
He did not follow the test procedure. 说"没遵守考试流程"，原文只字未提流程问题，
与"准备不足"这一真实原因无关。

questions.stem: What does the man say about his driving lessons?

explain.定位:
M: ... the lessons are rather expensive, £20 an hour. And the instructor says I'll need about 30
to 40 lessons in total. That's what—six to eight hundred pounds.
男：……这些课挺贵的，一小时 20 英镑。教练说我总共大概需要 30 到 40 节课。那大概是
——六百到八百英镑。
explain.信号:
形容词 expensive + 价格数字。答案句靠一个评价形容词加一串价格数字双重坐实：the
lessons are rather expensive, £20 an hour 直接说"贵"，又用 six to eight hundred
pounds 量化。听到对某物的形容词评价＋具体钱数，就是评价类细节题的答案信号。
explain.替换:
rather expensive ↔ costly
expensive=costly
£20 an hour ↔ costly
具体钱数佐证"贵"
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
They are tough. 说课"难"，但原文只说贵，没说上课难——男方反倒说 I'm really
enjoying it（很享受），与"难"相悖。
C) 过度推断
They are helpful. 说课"有帮助"，原文男方说享受、教练理解（my instructor is very
understanding），但没评价课"有用/有帮助"，是顺着"他挺喜欢"脑补的正面评价。
借用原文：my instructor is very understanding
D) 与原文相反
They are too short. 说课"太短"，但原文谈到的是数量多（30 to 40 lessons in total）和
贵，从未说每节课太短，方向相反。
借用原文：I'll need about 30 to 40 lessons in total

questions.stem: What does the man hope to do next?
options: A) Pass his road test the first time.
B) Test-drive a few times on highways.
C) Find an experienced driving instructor.
D) Earn enough money for driving lessons.

explain.定位:
M: ... So this time I'll need to make a lot more effort and hopefully will be successful the
first time.
男：……所以这次我得多下不少功夫，希望能一次就成功。
explain.信号:
this time + hopefully 表意图。答案句靠表意图的标志词锁定：this time I'll need to
make a lot more effort 与 hopefully will be successful the first time 中，this time、
hopefully、the first time 一齐出现，正是"下一步希望怎样"的信号；结合前文"下一步是路
考"，他希望的就是路考一次过。
explain.替换:
hopefully will be successful the first time ↔ Pass his road test the first time
成功一次过=一次过路考
the first time ↔ the first time
限定词原样对应
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
Test-drive a few times on highways. 里的 highways（高速）原文根本没出现，是凭空添
加的内容，与他"路考一次过"的目标无关。
C) 原词陷阱
Find an experienced driving instructor. 盗用了原文出现的 instructor，但男方说现在的
教练 very understanding、自己很享受，并无"另找有经验教练"之意，原词在、意思不
在。
借用原文：my instructor is very understanding
D) 过度推断
Earn enough money for driving lessons. 借第 10 题"课贵、六到八百镑"设套，但男方只

questions.stem: What does the man want to know?

how much it is for international students to study there ↔

explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
录音里 you're going to university in England 说的是女生在英国上学，A 项 Where the

B) 未提及
The acceptance rate at Leeds. 里 Leeds 录音确实念到，但男生问的是花多少钱，从没问

explain.信号:

这句当事人自述计划就是答案信号。
explain.替换:
doing my master's ↔ Pursue postgraduate studies.
读硕士=读研究生

A) 与原文相反

questions.stem: What might qualify the man for a scholarship at Leeds University?

Also, I have a good chance of winning a scholarship at Leeds, which would be pretty

因果短语 the benefits of。男生把"有望拿奖学金"归因于 the benefits of being a music

the plan is 自报计划。女生用 the plan is to work at an international school overseas
明确报出计划，the plan is… 这句"自报安排"就是答案信号，落点在"去海外国际学校

work at an international school overseas ↔ Teach overseas.

录音里 doing my master's 的硕士是男生的事；Do a master's degree. 把男生读硕士安到

Settle down in England. 盗用了 England，但录音说女生只是 after I get a year or so of
the experience in England（先在英国积累一年经验）就去海外，England 是过渡站不是

questions.stem: What does the passage say about ants?
options: A) They help farmers keep diseases in check.
B) Many species remain unknown to scientists.
C) Only a few species cause trouble to humans.
D) They live in incredibly well-organized colonies.

explain.定位:
Scientists have identified thousands of known ant species around the world—and only a few
of them bug humans.
科学家已在全球辨识出数以千计的已知蚂蚁种类——而其中只有少数会侵扰人类。
explain.信号:
数量对比 thousands 对 only a few。这句用破折号把 thousands of known ant species
和 only a few of them bug humans 摆成强烈对比，落点在 only a few 这个数量限定上，
正是题干要的关于蚂蚁的总括判断，凭这个数量对比信号即可锁定它是答案句。
explain.替换:
only a few of them bug humans ↔ Only a few species cause trouble to humans
bug 替换成 cause trouble
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音说蚂蚁在野外 keep other creatures in check（制衡其他生物），选项把它偷换成
help farmers keep diseases in check（帮农民控制病害），盗用了 keep…in check 这个
原词组，但对象从其他生物换成 diseases、还凭空安上 farmers，答非所问。
借用原文：keep other creatures in check
B) 未提及
Many species remain unknown to scientists. 说很多种类科学家还不知道，但录音只说科
学家已辨识出 thousands of known ant species（数以千计的已知种类），从没说还有很
多未知的，属无中生有；且 B 的 Many 与答案句 only a few 的数量取向正相反。
D) 原词陷阱
录音确实提到蚂蚁 live in colonies that number in the tens of thousands（群落数以万
计），但说的是数量庞大，并没说 well-organized（组织严密）。选项盗用 colonies 这个
原词，却替它加上录音没有的组织严密的评价，把数量多偷换成有组织。
借用原文：live in colonies that number in the tens of thousands

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about carpenter ants?
options: A) They are larger than many other species.
B) They can cause damage to people's homes.
C) They can survive a long time without water.
D) They like to form colonies in electrical units.

explain.定位:
Some, like carpenter ants, can undermine a home's structure, while others interfere with
electrical units.
有些蚂蚁，比如木匠蚁，会破坏房屋的结构，而另一些则会干扰电器设备。
explain.信号:
举例信号 like carpenter ants 直接点名。这句用 like carpenter ants 直接把木匠蚁拎出来
举例，紧跟的 undermine a home's structure（破坏房屋结构）就是它的专属描述；而句
中 while others 之后讲的是另一类蚂蚁，凭 like＋专名这个举例信号即可锁定前半句才是木
匠蚁的答案句。
explain.替换:
undermine a home's structure ↔ cause damage to people's homes
undermine structure 概括为 cause damage
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
They are larger than many other species. 说木匠蚁比许多种类大，但录音从头到尾没比
较过木匠蚁的体型，属无中生有；它利用了考生对木匠蚁（carpenter 听着像大块头）的常
识联想来骗选。
C) 原词陷阱
They can survive a long time without water. 说不喝水也能久活，录音讲蚂蚁时只说 our
homes are very attractive to ants, because they provide everything the colony needs
to survive, such as food, water, and shelter，提到 water 是说房屋能提供水，根本没说
蚂蚁能耐旱，属偷用 water 一词的无中生有。
借用原文：food, water, and shelter
D) 张冠李戴
录音确实说有蚂蚁 interfere with electrical units（干扰电器），但那是 while others 之后
讲的另一类蚂蚁，不是木匠蚁；选项 They like to form colonies in electrical units. 把别
种蚂蚁的电器危害安到木匠蚁头上，是典型张冠李戴，且 form colonies in 与 interfere
with 含义也不同。
借用原文：others interfere with electrical units

questions.stem: What can we do to prevent ants from getting into our homes?
options: A) Deny them access to any food.
B) Keep doors and windows shut.
C) Destroy their colonies close by.
D) Refrain from eating sugary food.

explain.定位:
Most important of all, avoid giving ants any access to food, particularly sugary food, because
ants have a sweet tooth.
最重要的是，别让蚂蚁有任何接触食物的机会，尤其是甜食，因为蚂蚁爱吃甜。
explain.信号:
强调信号 Most important of all 标出首要措施。Most important of all（最重要的是）
是明确的重要性强调信号，它后面紧跟的 avoid giving ants any access to food 就是录音
主推的首要办法，凭这个强调词即可锁定它是答案句，而非后面罗列的清理洒漏、密封储存
等次要措施。
explain.替换:
avoid giving ants any access to food ↔ Deny them access to any food
avoid giving access 等于 deny access
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音末尾提到把户外垃圾 well away from doors and windows（远离门窗存放），盗用了
doors and windows 这个原词，但说的是垃圾放远点、并非 Keep doors and windows
shut（关紧门窗），且这只是次要提醒，不是被强调的首要办法。
借用原文：well away from doors and windows
C) 未提及
Destroy their colonies close by. 说捣毁附近的蚂蚁群落，录音讲的防治全是断食源、清洒
漏、密封食物、清垃圾，从没说去捣毁群落，属无中生有；它利用 colonies 这个全篇高频
词制造熟悉感骗选。
借用原文：live in colonies that number in the tens of thousands
D) 偷换概念
录音说 particularly sugary food 时，是叮嘱别让蚂蚁接触食物、尤其甜食（管的是蚂蚁的
食源），选项 Refrain from eating sugary food. 却偷换成劝人自己别吃甜食，盗用
sugary food 原词却把约束对象从蚂蚁改成了人，答非所问。
借用原文：avoid giving ants any access to food, particularly sugary food

questions.stem: What is the focus of the speaker's research?
options: A) The function of the human immune system.
B) The cause of various auto-immune diseases.
C) The viruses that may infect the human immune system.
D) The change in people's immune system as they get older.

explain.定位:
My research focus is on what happens to our immune system as we age.
我的研究重点是，随着我们变老，免疫系统会发生什么变化。
explain.信号:
开头自报研究方向。答案句是录音第一句，说话人用 My research focus is on（我的研究
重点是）直接自报家门——这种"开门见山报主题"的句子就是主旨题的答案信号，不必等
后文。
explain.替换:
what happens to our immune system as we age ↔
The change in people's immune system as they get older
换词说同一件事
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确实念了 the job of the immune system is to fight infections，A 的 The function
of the human immune system. 借这个"功能"做诱饵；但"免疫系统的功能"只是讲述中的
一笔背景，研究的 focus 是"变老带来的变化"，A 把背景当成了主题。
借用原文：It also protects us from viruses and from auto-immune diseases
B) 原词陷阱
录音提到 from auto-immune diseases，B 的 The cause of various auto-immune
diseases. 就抓住 auto-immune 这个原词；但说话人只是把自身免疫病列为免疫系统要防
的东西之一，从没说要研究"它们的病因"，B 是无中生有地造了个研究方向。
借用原文：It also protects us from viruses and from auto-immune diseases
C) 原词陷阱
录音说 It also protects us from viruses，C 的 The viruses that may infect the human
immune system. 就借 viruses 设套；但原文是"免疫系统保护我们免受病毒"，C 却说成"研
究感染免疫系统的病毒"，方向反了也偏了，并非研究重点。
借用原文：So the job of the immune system is to fight infections

questions.stem: What are the volunteers asked to do in the research?

explain.定位:
They come to the university to provide us with blood samples, to be interviewed and to help
us carry out a whole range of research.
他们来到大学，为我们提供血样、接受访谈，并帮助我们开展一系列研究。
explain.信号:
列举志愿者所做之事。答案句紧跟在介绍 a great group of volunteers called "The 1,000
Elders" 之后，用 to provide us with blood samples, to be interviewed and to help us
一连串动词不定式列举志愿者做的事——这种"to do, to do and to do"的并列罗列就是细
节题的答案信号。
explain.替换:
to provide us with blood samples ↔ Offer blood samples
同义动词替换
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
录音说志愿者 to be interviewed（接受访谈），A 的 Report their illnesses.（报告病情）
听着像"被访谈"的内容，但原文从没说志愿者报告病情；而且这群 1,000 Elders 是健康对照
组，不是病人，没有病情可报。
C) 原词陷阱
录音说志愿者 to help us carry out a whole range of research（帮我们开展研究），C 的
Act as research assistants. 借 research 把"帮忙开展研究"夸大成"担任研究助理"；志愿者
是被研究、配合研究的对象，不是助理身份，C 把"帮忙"拔高成了"职务"。
借用原文：to help us carry out a whole range of research

录音说志愿者 to be interviewed（被访谈，是受访方），D 的 Help to interview
patients. 借 interview 这个原词，却把志愿者说成"帮忙访谈患者"（变成访谈方）；被访
vs 主访方向反了，且原文没提让志愿者去访谈病人。
借用原文：to be interviewed

questions.stem: What does the speaker say will be the impact of his research?
options: A) Strengthening people's immunity to infection.
B) Better understanding patients' immune system.
C) Helping improve old people's health conditions.
D) Further reducing old patients' medical expenses.

explain.定位:
The real impact of our research is going to be on health in old age.
我们研究真正的影响，将体现在老年期的健康上。
explain.信号:
原词 impact 直接点出。答案句直接用了题干同款词 The real impact of our research——
录音念出 impact 这个关键词，紧跟其后的 on health in old age 就是影响的具体落点，这
种"题干词原样出现"是细节题最强的定位信号。
explain.替换:
on health in old age ↔ Helping improve old people's health conditions
名词短语展开为动作描述
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音多次念 infection（如 fight infections、not spending time in hospital with
infections），A 的 Strengthening people's immunity to infection. 借 infection 设套；
但研究的 impact 是更上位的"老年健康"，"增强抗感染免疫力"只是手段之一，A 把整体影
响缩成了一个小点。
借用原文：not spending time in hospital with infections
B) 原词陷阱
录音通篇讲 immune system，B 的 Better understanding patients' immune system. 借
这个高频词；但"更好理解免疫系统"是研究的过程／内容，不是说话人所说的 impact（影
响落在老年健康上），B 把"研究内容"当成了"研究影响"。
借用原文：My research focus is on what happens to our immune system as we age

省钱"的常识脑补出来的，属原文未提。

么问，原文就用同一个动词把答案领出来。

a group of kids would get together to play chess ↔
A group of kids were playing chess after school

a couple of days after school ↔ after school

His students had trouble getting on with each other 说学生彼此关系差，但录音里有
trouble 一词其实出现在“老师自己”刚来时的困难上，并没有说学生之间相处不好，属于把

A lot of kids stayed at school to do their homework 借用了原文“放学后孩子们聚在学
校”这个背景，却把他们做的事从“下棋”偷换成“写作业”，原文根本没提 homework。

His students were struggling to follow his lessons 偷了原文里的 struggling 一词制造
“听到就想选”的诱惑，但原文 was struggling to connect with students 说的是老师难以
与学生建立联系，不是学生跟不上课。

questions.stem: What are dozens of students from Komada's school going to do this week?
options: A) Visit a chess team in Nashville.

D) Receive training for a chess competition.

to compete with about 5,000 other young people at the SuperNationals of chess.
而这周，数十名这样的学生正准备动身前往田纳西州的纳什维尔，与大约5000名其他年轻人
在国际象棋超级全国赛上同场竞技。
explain.信号:

到这个时间词就该立刻锁定这句——它正是交代“这周要做什么”的答案句。
explain.替换:
to compete with about 5,000 other young people at the SuperNationals of chess ↔

compete=participate in competition，SuperNationals=national
explain.排除:

questions.stem: An extended lifespan in the future will allow people to have more careers than now.
questions.passage:
How Work Will Change When Most of Us Live to 100

A) Today in the United States there are 72,000 centenarians(百岁老人). Worldwide, probably 450,000. If current trends continue, then by 2050 there will be more than a million in the US alone. According to the work of Professor James Vaupel and his co-researchers, 50% of babies born in the US in 2007 have a life expectancy of 104 or more. Broadly the same holds for the UK, Germany, France, Italy and Canada, and for Japan 50% of 2007 babies can expect to live to 107.

B) Understandably, there are concerns about what this means for public finances given the associated health and pension challenges. These challenges are real, and society urgently needs to address them. But it is also important to look at the wider picture of what happens when so many people live for 100 years. It is a mistake to simply equate longevity(长寿) with issues of old age. Longer lives have implications for all of life, not just the end of it.

C) Our view is that if many people are living for longer, and are healthier for longer, then this will result in an inevitable redesign of work and life. When people live longer, they are not only older for longer, but also younger for longer. There is some truth in the saying that "70 is the new 60" or "40 the new 30." If you age more slowly over a longer time period, then you are in some sense younger for longer.

D) But the changes go further than that. Take, for instance, the age at which people make commitments such as buying a house, getting married, having children, or starting a career. These are all fundamental commitments that are now occurring later in life. In 1962, 50% of Americans were married by age 21. By 2014, that milestone(里程碑) had shifted to age 29.

E) While there are numerous factors behind these shifts, one factor is surely a growing realization for the young that they are going to live longer. Options are more valuable the longer they can be held. So if you believe you will live longer, then options become more valuable, and early commitment becomes less attractive. The result is that the commitments that previously characterized the beginning of adulthood are now being delayed, and new patterns of behavior and a new stage of life are emerging for those in their twenties.

F) Longevity also pushes back the age of retirement, and not only for financial reasons. Yes, unless people are prepared to save a lot more, our calculations suggest that if you are now in your mid-40s, then you are likely to work until your early 70s; and if you are in your early 20s, there is a real chance you will need to work until your late 70s or possibly even into your 80s. But even if people are able to economically support a retirement at 65, over thirty years of potential inactivity is harmful to cognitive(认知的) and emotional vitality. Many people may simply not want to do it.

G) And yet that does not mean that simply extending our careers is appealing. Just lengthening that second stage of full-time work may secure the financial assets needed for a 100-year life, but such persistent work will inevitably exhaust precious intangible assets such as productive skills, vitality, happiness, and friendship.

H) The same is true for education. It is impossible that a single shot of education, administered in childhood and early adulthood, will be able to support a sustained, 60-year career. If you factor in the projected rates of technological change, either your skills will become unnecessary, or your industry outdated. That means that everyone will, at some point in their life, have to make a number of major reinvestments in their skills.

I) It seems likely, then, that the traditional three-stage life will evolve into multiple stages containing two, three, or even more different careers. Each of these stages could potentially be different. In one the focus could be on building financial success and personal achievement, in another on creating a better work/life balance, still another on exploring and understanding options more fully, or becoming an independent producer, yet another on making a social contribution. These stages will span sectors, take people to different cities, and provide foundation for building a wide variety of skills.

J) Transitions between stages could be marked with sabbaticals(休假) as people find time to rest and recharge their health, re-invest in their relationships, or improve their skills. At times, these breaks and transitions will be self-determined, at others they will be forced as existing roles, firms, or industries cease to exist.

K) A multi-stage life will have profound changes not just in how you manage your career, but also in your approach to life. An increasingly important skill will be your ability to deal with change and even welcome it. A three-stage life has few transitions, while a multi-stage life has many. That is why being self-aware, investing in broader networks of friends, and being open to new ideas will become even more crucial skills.

L) These multi-stage lives will create extraordinary variety across groups of people simply because there are so many ways of sequencing the stages. More stages mean more possible sequences.

M) With this variety will come the end of the close association of age and stage. In a three-stage life, people leave university at the same time and the same age, they tend to start their careers and family at the same age, they proceed through middle management all roughly the same time, and then move into retirement within a few years of each other. In a multi-stage life, you could be an undergraduate at 20, 40, or 60; a manager at 30, 50, or 70; and become an independent producer at any age.

N) Current life structures, career paths, educational choices, and social norms are out of tune with the emerging reality of longer lifespans. The three-stage life of full-time education, followed by continuous work, and then complete retirement may have worked for our parents or even grandparents, but it is not relevant today. We believe that to focus on longevity as primarily an issue of aging is to miss its full implications. Longevity is not necessarily about being older for longer. It is about living longer, being older later, and being younger longer.

questions.stem: How might people often feel when they were misnamed?
questions.passage:
If you were like most children, you probably got upset when your mother called you by a sibling's(兄弟姐妹的) name. How could she not know you? Did it mean she loved you less?

Probably not. According to the first research to tackle this topic head-on, misnaming the most familiar people in our life is a common cognitive(认知的) error that has to do with how our memories classify and store familiar names.

The study, published online in April in the journal Memory and Cognition, found that the "wrong" name is not random but is invariably fished out from the same relationship pond: children, siblings, friends. The study did not examine the possibility of deep psychological significance to the mistake, says psychologist David Rubin, "but it does tell us who's in and who's out of the group."

The study also found that within that group, misnamings occurred where the names shared initial or internal sounds, like Jimmy and Joanie or John and Bob. Physical resemblance between people was not a factor. Nor was gender.

The researchers conducted five separate surveys of more than 1,700 people. Some of the surveys included only college students; others were done with a mixed-age population. Some asked subjects about incidents where someone close to them—family or friend—had called them by another person's name. The other surveys asked about times when subjects had themselves called someone close to them by the wrong name.
